revisions.owner_action: Settings -> Developer -> Boot: toggle Verbose boot on, then reboot once and confirm the boot log appears on the glass before the launcher; disable it again. The one-time Bixby-hold override is BLOCKED_KERNEL/BOOT_UPDATE_REQUIRED and cannot be tested (docs/beta-finalization/manual-proof/03-display-boot.md step 5)
revisions.note: Durable setting at /etc/nuxel/boot/verbose-boot.json (shipped default in configs/nuxel/boot/verbose-boot.json), installed with the 'keep' upgrade rule and merged on every write so a package update can never clobber a user decision; legacy flags migrated once. Honoured by the early userspace stage (nuxel-verbose-boot.service -> nuxel-verbose-boot.py), toggleable from the Quick Settings tile and the Settings app, and wired into 'nuxelctl verbose-boot status|on|off|override'. The one-time Bixby-hold override is implemented but the installed early boot stage cannot read the Bixby key state, so it is honestly reported as BLOCKED_KERNEL / BOOT_UPDATE_REQUIRED and REFUSED rather than faked behind a cosmetic switch. On-glass effect remains NEEDS_OWNER_TEST.

revisions.owner_action: Settings -> Developer -> Boot diagnostics: set the animation to off, reboot once (no animation, launcher appears directly), set it back to standard; then verbosity 0 vs 3 with verbose boot ON, reboot once each and compare the appended block in /var/log/nuxel/boot-stage.log. The one-time Bixby-hold override remains BLOCKED_KERNEL/BOOT_UPDATE_REQUIRED and is untestable (docs/beta-finalization/manual-proof/03-display-boot.md steps 5/5b/5c)
revisions.note: Revision 3 (bg-02 verification pass). The briQ asked for Settings -> Developer -> Boot Diagnostics = standard animation + persistent verbose boot + verbosity level, all persisted - revision 2 shipped only the verbose-boot toggle, so the other two controls are NEW here and are real, not cosmetic: (1) animation_mode (standard|short|off) with the ONE precedence rule off > short > verbose_boot > standard, implemented once in the boot-time consumer and asserted in two suites; (2) verbosity_level 0..3, which selects HOW MUCH the boot log says and never whether it is shown. All three live in the SAME durable document (/etc/nuxel/boot/verbose-boot.json, still schema_version 1 because the change is purely additive, which is what makes a downgrade safe), are written by the Settings panel, the Quick Settings tile and nuxelctl verbose-boot animation|verbosity through one merge-on-write path each, and are read by nuxel-verbose-boot.service, which now publishes EFFECTIVE_ANIMATION/ANIMATION_REASON/VERBOSITY plus the NUXEL_BOOT_ANIMATION marker and names the reason in /run/nuxel/anim-skip.request. An unknown animation_mode or an out-of-range verbosity is REPORTED and never silently reinterpreted. The one-time Bixby hold stays BLOCKED_KERNEL/BOOT_UPDATE_REQUIRED with an explicit userspace fallback (nuxelctl/Settings toggle) recorded in the document itself. On-glass effect remains NEEDS_OWNER_TEST.
